Benefitsofbiophilicdesign
Biophilicdesignseekstocreatebuiltenvironmentsthatpromoteaconnection
withnature,suchasincorporatingnaturallight,plants,andwaterfeaturesinto
buildingdesign.Connectednesswithnaturehasbeenshowntohavevarious
psychological, physiological, and social benefits, such as reducing stress,
improving cognitive function, enhancing overall well-being, and increasing
self-esteem.17 Connecting with nature can also increase physical activity and
lower obesity rates.18 From a social point of view, interpersonal interactions,
social engagement, and social cohesion among people increase when they
areexposedtonature.19
Biophilicdesignelementsandapproaches
The biophilic design framework developed by Stephen Kellert and Elizabeth
Calabreseconsistsofthreecategoriesofnatureexperiences:directexperience
ofnature,indirectexperienceofnature,andexperienceofspaceandplace.20
Directexperienceofnatureinvolvesphysicalcontactwithnaturalelementsin
the built environment while indirect experience of nature involves contact
with the agents or images of nature and patterns that represent the natural
world. Experience of space and place focuses on spatial features with the
characteristics of natural environments.21 Terrapin Bright Green emphasises
threeclassificationsofuserexperience:‘nature inthespace,naturalanalogs,
and nature of the space’.22 Direct contact with nature, including auditory,
visual, tactile and olfactory experiences of nature, has significant impact on
people.23
Biophilicdesignelementsincludelight,air,water,plants,animals,fire,land-
scape,weather,andnaturalviews,whichcanbeimplementedthroughthree
approaches: physical connection with nature, visual connection with nature,
and auditory connection with nature.24 Physical connection with nature is
themoststraightforwardapproach,anditinvolvesdirectlyincorporatingbiophi-
lic design elements in the built environment, such as water features, green
space, green walls, and fireplaces.25 Visual connection with nature involves
incorporating design elements that help people visually experience nature,
such as paintings of natural scenes or animals, views toward green space,
using natural materials such as woods and stones, and even using green
colour in decoration, which symbolises vegetation.26 Auditory connection
with nature involves experiencing nature-related sounds in built environment

conclusions. In many research contexts, especially in social sciences and
surveys,datamaynotbecontinuousornormallydistributed.61Non-parametric
testsarespecificallydesignedtohandlesuchdata,makingthemsuitablefora
widerangeofresearchscenarios.
